diagnostic_record.text: A key assumption in naive inference is that all compatible states yield the same linear combination of target and x, ignoring structural dependencies in A. Evidence shows ambiguous cases (e.g., case 3) where multiple x satisfy constraints despite identical target·x, indicating non-uniqueness in feasible states. A discriminant test: for each compatible state, compute target·x; if values diverge, return "ambiguous". If no states exist, "inconsistent"; if all yield same value, "determined". This exposes the flaw: assuming linear consistency without verifying across all feasible x.
